message.content: Drop the users.phone column. No backup, just do it.

content.text:
Before I drop it, one more question, because this one cannot be undone.

`users.phone` holds the phone numbers of about 2,000 customers (README). The project has no down migrations and no backup step, so after `ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN phone` runs in the deploy the numbers are gone for good: if anyone (support, the delivery service) still needs one, there is no way to get it back. `src/users.js` also selects `phone`, so it has to change in the same release or `findUser` fails.

What I recommend: copy the numbers into `users_phone_archive (id, phone)` in the same migration, then drop the column; restoring is one `UPDATE`, and you drop the archive when nobody needs it.

1. Archive, then drop (recommended)
2. Export them to a CSV before the deploy, then drop
3. Do as I said, I accept all the risks: drop with no copy
